answer: Physical uniqueness beats cheap wallets. Each new account must complete a one-time check-in at a public landmark, for example a harbor jetty or a trailhead in open karst country, and broadcast a short-range signal that nearby witnesses countersign. Because a person cannot stand in two places at the same minute, an attacker who wants a thousand accounts has to hire a thousand travelers, pay their time and transport, and risk those witnesses refusing a repeat face. The cost is labor and logistics, not another generated key.
